title: Folded Atlas
style: Cinematic jazz with brushed drums, upright bass walking in loose syncopation, smoky piano voicings, and muted trumpet replies; verse stays intimate and sparse, pre-chorus opens with strings and ride-cymbal lift, chorus blooms with stacked harmonies and a sustained horn line. Lead vocal is close-mic and hushed in verses, then doubled and breathy on the hook. Vinyl hiss, reverse piano swell, and a soft tom roll bridge the sections. Wide, dark, and velvet-smooth mix with polished low end., jazz
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I found your map in my coat
Creased at the edges, soft with rain
Every street was half erased
Every corner wore your name

I held it up to the glass
Nothing there but moving frames
Trains slid by like silver knives
And I still read the same

[Pre-Chorus]
Tell me where to go
If the ink won't stay
Tell me which way home
When the towns drift away

[Chorus]
Lost in transit
Lost in transit
No place to land

Lost in transit
Lost in transit
Map in my hand

[Verse 2]
Platform seven, midnight tea
Red cap rolling through the hall
I traced the coast in shaking light
But the ocean wouldn't call

A child slept on a suitcase lid
Old man hummed through broken teeth
Every stop was borrowed time
Every mile a folded grief

[Pre-Chorus]
Tell me where to go
If the ink won't stay
Tell me which way home
When the towns drift away

[Chorus]
Lost in transit
Lost in transit
No place to land

Lost in transit
Lost in transit
Map in my hand

[Bridge]
Maybe I was never meant
For a pin or fixed address
Maybe all I carry now
Is this beautiful unrest

So I fold it slow
Put the rain back in
If there's nowhere left to reach
Let the journey win

[Chorus]
Lost in transit
Lost in transit
No place to land

Lost in transit
Lost in transit
Map in my hand
